cls: PI3K-alpha specific inhibitor and catalytic degrader (kinase inhibitor)
pharm: Inhibitor of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) with activity predominantly against PI3K-alpha; induces degradation of mutated p110-alpha, blocks AKT phosphorylation, and inhibits growth of PIK3CA-mutated breast cancer, used with palbociclib and fulvestrant
quick: 9 mg orally once daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity
With or without food at about the same time daily
Can cause fetal harm; verify status; effective non-hormonal contraception during and for 1 week after last dose
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose
Moderate impairment (eGFR 30 to <60): start 6 mg daily; mild: no change; severe: not evaluated
Mild: no clinically significant PK difference; moderate-severe: unknown
No specific interaction; limit use during therapy
Fasting glucose/HbA1c, stomatitis, diarrhea/hydration, CBC, electrolytes, renal function, pregnancy status
summary: Inavolisib (Itovebi) is an oral PI3K-alpha specific inhibitor and catalytic degrader used with palbociclib and fulvestrant for adults with endocrine-resistant, PIK3CA-mutated, HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after recurrence on or after adjuvant endocrine therapy, based on the INAVO120 trial. The dose is 9 mg once daily with or without food (6 mg daily starting dose in moderate renal impairment). It can cause severe or fatal hyperglycemia including ketoacidosis: check fasting glucose and HbA1c, optimize glucose before starting, and interrupt, reduce, or stop for severe hyperglycemia. Severe stomatitis and severe diarrhea with dehydration and kidney injury, plus embryo-fetal toxicity, are key risks. There are no absolute contraindications in labeling.
indications: In combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant for adults with endocrine-resistant, PIK3CA-mutated, HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, as detected by an FDA-approved test, following recurrence on or after completing adjuvant endocrine therapy

dosage.t: Once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Give with palbociclib 125 mg daily 21 of 28 days plus fulvestrant per their labels; select by PIK3CA mutation in plasma

dosage.d: Starting dose 6 mg once daily (eGFR 30 to <60 mL/min)
dosage.n: No change for mild impairment (eGFR 60 to <90); not evaluated in severe impairment

dosage.d: First reduction to 6 mg daily, second reduction to 3 mg daily
dosage.t: Once daily after interruption for the adverse reaction
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue if not tolerated at 3 mg daily or for recurrent severe toxicity; see label tables for hyperglycemia, stomatitis, and diarrhea management

dosage.d: Take a missed dose within 9 hours; skip if more than 9 hours
dosage.n: Do not take an extra dose after vomiting; resume the usual schedule the next day

admin: Take once daily at about the same time, with or without food; swallow tablets whole
Available as 3 mg and 9 mg tablets; 9 mg dose may use one 9 mg tablet
Check fasting glucose and HbA1c and optimize blood glucose before starting
Start antidiarrheals, fluids, and clinician contact at first severe diarrhea; consider corticosteroid mouthwash for stomatitis per labeling
Verify pregnancy status before starting; use effective non-hormonal contraception
moa: Inavolisib inhibits phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) with activity predominantly against PI3K-alpha. In vitro it induces degradation of the mutated catalytic subunit p110-alpha encoded by PIK3CA, inhibits phosphorylation of downstream AKT, reduces proliferation, and induces apoptosis in PIK3CA-mutated breast cancer lines; in vivo it slowed growth of PIK3CA-mutated ER-positive xenografts. Combined with palbociclib and fulvestrant it increased tumor growth inhibition versus single agents or doublets.

relative: Diabetes or poor glycemic control (severe or fatal hyperglycemia risk)
History of severe stomatitis or severe diarrhea with dehydration risk
monitor: Fasting glucose and HbA1c before and during treatment
Mouth for stomatitis; stool pattern, hydration, and renal function

preg: Based on animal data and mechanism, inavolisib can cause fetal harm. In rats dosed during organogenesis, exposures near the human 9 mg/day AUC caused embryo-fetal death, structural defects (including vertebral, thoracic arch, and eye defects), lower viability, and growth reduction. There are no human pregnancy data. Verify pregnancy status before starting. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose; advise males with partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Refer to palbociclib and fulvestrant labels for their pregnancy and contraception information.
lact: There are no data on inavolisib in human milk or its effects on the child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious reactions, advise lactating women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
renal: Reduce the starting dose to 6 mg once daily in moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30 to <60 mL/min). No change for mild impairment (eGFR 60 to <90). Not evaluated in severe impairment (eGFR <30); use with caution and monitor closely. Severe diarrhea can cause dehydration and acute kidney injury regardless of baseline function.
hepatic: No clinically significant PK difference was seen in mild hepatic impairment (TB >ULN to 1.5 x ULN, or AST >ULN with TB <=ULN). The effect of moderate to severe hepatic impairment is unknown; use with caution and monitor.

major: Sensitive CYP3A substrates - inavolisib induces CYP3A and CYP2B6 and is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, so substrate exposure may change; monitor and adjust
P-gp or BCRP modulators - inavolisib is a P-gp and BCRP substrate, so strong modulators may alter its exposure; follow labeling
moderate: Antihyperglycemic agents - initiation or optimization is commonly needed; adjust diabetes therapy to glucose trends
Myelosuppressive partners (palbociclib) - additive cytopenias; monitor CBC
minor: Minimal CYP3A metabolism (primarily hydrolysis) suggests limited effect of CYP3A inhibitors on inavolisib, but follow labeling; no inhibition of CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, or 2D6
interactions.food: Take with or without food; no clinically significant food effect described
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; limit alcohol during cancer therapy
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor fasting glucose, HbA1c, CBC (neutrophils, hemoglobin, platelets, lymphocytes), calcium, potassium, creatinine, ALT, sodium, magnesium

common: Decreased appetite, calcium, potassium, sodium, magnesium
serious: Severe or fatal hyperglycemia including ketoacidosis
Severe diarrhea with dehydration and acute kidney injury
Severe cytopenias with infection or bleeding (with palbociclib combination)
rare: Impaired fertility in females and males (animal finding)
Severe cutaneous reactions with combination therapy (monitor rash)
emergency: DKA symptoms (excessive thirst, frequent urination, fruity breath, confusion) - seek urgent care
Severe diarrhea with dizziness, low urine output, or fainting
Mouth sores preventing eating or drinking, fever, or signs of infection

monitoring: Fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c before starting and periodically; optimize glucose and start or adjust antihyperglycemics
Mouth exams for stomatitis; withhold, reduce, or stop by severity
Stool frequency, hydration, and creatinine for diarrhea; start antidiarrheals and fluids early
CBC and metabolic panel (electrolytes, creatinine, ALT, calcium, magnesium)
Pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential
counsel: Take 9 mg once daily at about the same time, with or without food; if you miss a dose take it within 9 hours, otherwise skip it
High blood sugar can be severe or fatal: know DKA symptoms, take diabetes medicines as directed, and attend glucose checks
Report mouth sores, diarrhea (start antidiarrheal and fluids and call for severe cases), rash, unusual fatigue, fever, or signs of infection
Use effective non-hormonal birth control during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose (partners too for males); do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after
You will also take palbociclib and fulvestrant; follow their schedules and tell the team about all other medicines
pk: Target inhibition with daily dosing; steady-state concentrations predicted by day 5; tumor response accrues over weeks
Geometric mean steady-state Cmax about 69 ng/mL; steady-state AUC about 1010 h*ng/mL
Elimination half-life about 15 hours; total clearance about 8.8 L/h
Once-daily dosing maintains steady state from about day 5; continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F), excursions 15-30 C permitted; keep in original container tightly closed to protect from moisture
pearls: PI3K-alpha specific inhibitor plus catalytic degrader of mutated p110-alpha, paired with CDK4/6 and endocrine blockade in PIK3CA-mutated HR-positive HER2-negative disease (INAVO120)
Hyperglycemia can be severe or fatal including ketoacidosis: baseline FPG/HbA1c plus optimization is required, not optional
Diarrhea can precipitate AKI: early antidiarrheals, fluids, and interruption/reduction rules matter
Moderate renal impairment starts at 6 mg daily; toxicity reductions step 9 to 6 to 3 mg
Non-hormonal contraception during and for 1 week after (females and male partners); no breastfeeding during and for 1 week after
missed: Take a missed dose as soon as possible within 9 hours. If more than 9 hours have passed, skip it and take the next dose at the scheduled time. If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not take an extra dose that day; resume the usual schedule the next day.
overdose: No specific treatment for inavolisib overdose is described. Manage with supportive care and monitoring for exaggerated effects such as hyperglycemia, stomatitis, diarrhea with dehydration, and cytopenias, including glucose, hydration, CBC, and renal function. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
